title: Launch, Optimization, and Basic Analytics

teach.title: Why a checklist is critically important
teach.body: Mistakes made before launch cost more than those made afterward. If you launch a campaign with a malfunctioning pixel or an incorrect postback, your entire budget will be spent without a single conversion being credited. Spending 15 minutes on a check can save you $100–200 of your test budget.

teach.title: Technical Section
teach.body:
**Account and Security:**
- [ ] Account purchased, set up, and fully configured (see Module 09 for details)
- [ ] Anti-detection browser configured; profile loaded with the correct settings
- [ ] The proxy matches the account’s GEO (Polish account = Polish or neutral proxy)
- [ ] Business Manager and the ad account are active; there are no restrictions

**Payment:**
- [ ] The card is linked to the ad account
- [ ] The card has sufficient funds (at least the current billing threshold × 2)
- [ ] Make sure the card hasn’t been declined recently

**Fan Page:**
- [ ] The Fan Page is complete: profile picture, cover photo, description, contact information
- [ ] There are posts (at least 3–5 posts)
- [ ] The Fan Page’s theme matches the offer

teach.title: Land and Tracking
teach.body:
**Pixel:**
- [ ] The pixel is installed on the landing page (verify via Pixel Helper or Events Manager)
- [ ] The Lead or Purchase event is triggered on the correct page (the "thank you" page)
- [ ] Submit a test request and verify that the event is recorded in Events Manager
- [ ] If there is a tracker, make sure clicks and conversions are being tracked correctly

**Landing Page:**
- [ ] The landing page loads in 3 seconds or less (check Google PageSpeed)
- [ ] The domain has been verified via the Facebook Sharing Debugger—no errors or bans
- [ ] The mobile version is correct: the CTA button is visible without scrolling, and the form is user-friendly
- [ ] Test application: data was received in the affiliate network’s CRM (most important!)
- [ ] Message Match between the creative and the landing page

**Offer:**
- [ ] The offer is active in the affiliate network (not paused)
- [ ] The cap has not been exhausted as of today
- [ ] Links with UTM tags or postbacks are configured correctly

teach.title: Campaign Settings
teach.body:
- [ ] The campaign objective is correct (for this ad—Sales)
- [ ] The audience has been set up or verified
- [ ] The budget and bidding strategy have been set (ABO, Lowest Cost for testing)
- [ ] Creatives have been uploaded in the correct formats (4:5 for Feed, 9:16 for Stories)
- [ ] Planned start time and end date (if applicable)

teach.title: First check after startup (1–2 hours later)
teach.body:
- Ads have the "Active" status (not "In Review" or "Rejected")
- There are initial impressions and clicks
- The pixel is tracking PageViews
- Spend is in line with the budget (not zero and not abnormally high)

l1.q: 80 clicks per day but 0 conversions in the affiliate program. The pixel shows 12 lead events. What most likely happened?
options: The audience is irrelevant
The postback between the landing page and the affiliate program is configured incorrectly—leads are not being tracked
The affiliate program is delaying the display of conversions
Creo does not convert

l1.q: What steps should be taken with the landing page before each launch of a new offer?
options: Change the button's color
Submit a test request and verify that the data has been sent to the affiliate program's CRM
Add fields for data collection
Check the form's loading speed

l2.situation:
Situation:
A media buyer is preparing to launch an ad campaign in Poland:
- Account: Polish, pre-populated ✓
- Anti-detection: uploaded ✓
- Proxy: mobile, UKRAINE ✗
- Card: Polish, balance $50 ✓
- Pixel: installed but no test request was sent ✗
- Landing page: speed 2.1 sec ✓, no test request was sent ✗

questions.q: What needs to be fixed before launch?
options: The proxy must be Polish or neutral
The card needs to be changed to a Ukrainian one
Be sure to submit a test request and verify that the data was received
Check pixel functionality using a test conversion

questions.q: Why is a GEO proxy so important?
options: Facebook shows ads only in GEO proxy
A Polish account with a Ukrainian IP address — suspicious login, risk of verification or a ban
Ukrainian proxies are being blocked by Polish advertisers
This only affects the speed of the office

lessons.title: Day One: What to Look At and What to Leave Alone

teach.title: Why Is the First Day Special?
teach.body:
The first day is the hardest psychologically. There are no conversions, and you feel the urge to change something. But it’s precisely on the first day that those who “do something” cause the most damage.

Facebook’s algorithm enters the learning phase [→ Lesson 5.6]. Spending is uneven. The CPA on the first day is almost always worse than it will be on days 2–3. There may be no conversions at all, and that’s normal.

teach.title: What to Watch
teach.body:
**Ad Status:**
30–60 minutes after launch, all ads should be "Active." If they’re "Rejected," read the reason and fix it. If they’re "In Review," wait—usually up to 24 hours.

**Are costs being incurred?**
If there are 0 impressions and 0 costs after 2–3 hours, something is wrong. Possible reasons: the account is restricted, the card was declined, the audience is too narrow, or the campaign hasn’t launched.

**CTR:**
After 500–1,000 impressions, the CTR gives the first indication of how well the creative is performing. Below 0.5% with 1,000+ impressions means the creative isn’t converting well. Above 1.5% is a good sign.

**PageView:**
The pixel should track PageView events. If there are clicks but no PageViews, there’s a problem with the redirect or the pixel.

teach.title: What NOT to Do
teach.body:
- Pause the ad set after 0 conversions in the first few hours
- Change the audience, creative, or budget on the first day (except in extreme cases)
- Increase the budget "to speed up learning"
- Panic over a poor CPA on the first day

teach.title: The only exception for early intervention
teach.body:
**CTR below 0.3% with 1,000+ impressions** — the creative clearly isn’t catching anyone’s attention. In this case, you can replace the creative without waiting until the next day.

**Non-targeted leads from day one** — if the first leads are clearly off-target (different age, different problem, invalid phone numbers) — turn it off and give the auto-rule a second chance. The algorithm learns from those who converted—non-targeted leads will teach it to seek out even more non-targeted leads.

**The Half-Budget Rule:**
Before turning off an ad set due to a lack of leads, it must have spent at least half of the daily budget. At $10/day, that’s a minimum of $5 in spending before drawing any conclusions.

l1.q: Day 1: Spent $8 out of $10, CTR 2.4%, 0 conversions. Correct action:
options: Turn off — clearly doesn't work
Don't change anything—the CTR is good, and 0 conversions on the first day is normal
Replace the creosote
Increase the budget to $20

l1.q: At what CTR and number of impressions can you replace the creative as early as the first day?
options: CTR of 1.5% with 500 impressions
A CTR of 0.2% with 1,000+ impressions—the ad clearly isn't holding back
CTR of 0% with 100 impressions
3% CTR with 200 impressions

questions.q: What are you doing with Adset B?
options: You're waiting until tomorrow
If you replace the creative—a CTR of 0.18% on 3,400 impressions means the creative isn't stopping anyone
You're increasing the budget
Changing your audience

questions.q: What are you doing with Adset D?
options: Turn it off—low costs
No problem—$0.8 in expenses is too small a figure to draw any conclusions
You're increasing the budget
Changing your audience

questions.q: Adset B — 1 conversion at $5.1 with a payout of $6. What do you do?
options: You can scale it right away
Leave it and wait until the next day—a single conversion isn't a trend
If you turn it off, one conversion isn't enough
You're doing a remake with a bigger budget

lessons.title: The Two-Day Rule and Traffic Rules

teach.title: The Two-Day Rule
teach.body:
**The Two-Day Rule:** The decision to permanently disable an ad set is made only after two full business days of poor results.

Why two days:
- The first day is always unstable due to the learning phase
- Results can vary significantly depending on the day of the week
- The algorithm needs at least 2 days to start finding its audience

**Exception:** If the CTR is below 0.3% with 1,000+ impressions, the ad is underperforming and can be paused earlier [→ Lesson 8.2].

teach.title: AutoRules — Basic Automation
teach.body:
Facebook’s automated rules allow you to set conditions under which the system automatically performs an action. This eliminates the need for nighttime monitoring.

**A basic automated rule to start with:**
"Turn on all ad sets in the campaign at 12:00 a.m. every day"

Logic: If you turned off an ad set during the day due to poor results, the automation rule will give it a second chance the next day with a fresh budget. You don’t have to log in at night, but the ad set will start fresh.

Settings in Ads Manager: Automations → Create Automation Rule → condition / action / schedule.

teach.title: Practical Workflow Diagram
teach.body:
**Day 1, 2:00 PM:** >50% of the budget spent, 0 leads, good CTR.
Action: Turn off ADS (not ad sets). An automated rule will turn on the ad set at 12:00 AM—it will start tomorrow with a new daily budget.

**Day 2, morning:** Check the results for the second day.
- There are leads and the CPA is acceptable → leave it running, monitor
- There are leads but the CPA is poor → run for one more day or pause, depending on the trend
- 0 leads again → pause permanently or send it for rework

teach.title: Level-based shutdown logic
teach.body:
Always pause at the minimum necessary level:

- A specific ad is performing poorly → pause the ad (leave the ad set active)
- The entire ad set is performing poorly → pause the ad set (leave the campaign active)
- The entire campaign is underperforming → pause the campaign

An automated rule can turn on the ad set at 12:00 a.m. However, if the campaign is paused, there will be no spend even if the ad set is active. Manage this at the top level.

l1.q: Why is the decision to disable the ad set made after two days?
options: Facebook requires at least two days
The first day is unreliable due to training; the second day provides more representative data
Two days is the minimum required for statistical significance
Rule from affiliate networks

l1.q: MediaBuyer paused the ad at 3:00 p.m. Avtopravilo will resume the ad at 12:00 a.m. But the entire campaign is paused. What will happen?
options: The Traffic Police will also launch a campaign
AdSet will be enabled, but there will be no charges as long as the campaign is disabled
The auto-correct feature won't work
The campaign will start automatically

l2.situation:
Scenario — two days, $10/day, payout upon approval of $5.5:

| Ad Set | Day 1 | Day 2 |
|-------|--------|--------|
| A | $9.8, 0 leads | $9.5, 0 leads |
| B | $9.2, 1 lead ($9.2) | $9.7, 2 leads ($4.85/lead) |
| C | $8.1, 2 leads ($4.05) | $9.3, 3 leads ($3.1) |
| D | $9.4, 0 leads | $9.6, 1 lead ($9.6) |

questions.q: Adset A — two days, 0 leads. What do you do?
options: One more day
Turn it off—two days without leads, even with a full budget, is enough to draw a conclusion
You're increasing the budget
Change the audience and two more days

questions.q: Adset B — improvement ($4.05 → $3.1). What are you doing?
options: Turn it off
Leave it as is and let's see—there's a positive trend, and the CPA is lower than the payout
You immediately double your budget
You're repeating yourself

questions.q: Adset G — Day 1: 0 leads; Day 2: 1 lead at $9.6 with a payout of $5.5. What do you do?
options: If you leave it, there's a conversion
If you turn it off—two days later, the CPA is almost twice as high as the payout, with no sign of improvement
Two more days
You're switching leads to another offer

lessons.title: Reading Metrics: What to Look At and in What Order

teach.title: Metrics Funnel
teach.body:
When CPA is poor, the question is, “Where exactly is the problem?” The answer is to read the metrics funnel from left to right:

```
CPM → CTR → CPC → CR → CPA → ROI
```

Each metric depends on the one before it. If you know where it went wrong, you know what to fix.

teach.title: Analysis Algorithm
teach.body:
**Step 1: CPM**
Compare it to the expected CPM for this GEO and vertical. A sharp increase in CPM with the same settings is a sign of increased competition or audience burnout (high frequency).

**Step 2: CTR**
Below 0.5–0.8% with 1,000+ impressions—possibly weak creative or an irrelevant audience. Above 1.5%—the creative is performing well. Above 3%—excellent.

**Step 3: CPC**
Depends on CPM and CTR. If CPC is too high with a normal CPM, it means CTR is low.

**Step 4: Landing Page CR**
If the CTR is good but there are no conversions or very few—the problem lies with the landing page or Message Match. The actual CR is calculated as conversions / clicks × 100%.

**Step 5: CPA**
If the CPA is lower than the actual payout (payout × approval rate), you’re making a profit. If it’s higher, you’re losing money.

**Step 6: ROI**
The overall result for the week or month.

teach.title: Diagnosis Using the Funnel Method
teach.body:
| Situation | Where the problem lies |
|----------|-------------|
| Poor CTR with normal CPM | Creative or audience |
| Good CTR but poor CR | Landing page or Message Match |
| Good CR but poor CPA | High CPM or narrow audience |
| Good CPA but poor ROI | Low approval rate or payout too low |

l1.q: CTR 3.1%, landing page CR 0.4%, CPA $35 with a payout of $8. What's the problem?
options: In Creo, the CTR is poor
In a landing page or Message Match—the creative stops users, but the landing page doesn't convert
The audience consists of irrelevant traffic
CPM involves expensive impressions

l1.q: CPM rose from $4 to $12 per week with the same settings. The most likely reason:
options: Facebook has changed its algorithm
The audience is overheated (high frequency) or competition in the auction has increased
Creos has become of lower quality
Land is loading slowly

l2.situation:
The situation: three ad sets, the same audience and landing page, different creatives, $8 payout:

| Metric | Ad Set A | Ad Set B | Ad Set C |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| CPM | $5.2 | $5.1 | $5.3 |
| CTR | 0.4% | 2.9% | 2.7% |
| CPC | $1.30 | $0.18 | $0.20 |
| CR | 3.1% | 0.3% | 3.0% |
| CPA | $41.9 | $60 | $6.7 |

questions.q: What's the problem with Adseti A?
options: Poor landing CR
A poor CTR isn't stopping the ad campaign, which is why the CPC is $1.30 and the CPA is $41.9
Dear CPM
Low payout

questions.q: What's the problem with Adseti B?
options: Low CTR
Good CTR but very low CR—the creative catches people's attention, but the landing page or Message Match is driving them away
Dear CPM
No problem—a CPC of $0.18 is great
Turn off all three and look for a new offer
Scale up B, turn off A and B, analyze why version B is better, and create similar ones
You're increasing the budget for all three
Give Adset A and B another week

lessons.title: Maximum Lead Cost and Decision-Making Logic

teach.title: Why the average CPA Doesn't Tell the Whole Story
teach.body:
"Average CPA per day" can mask the real situation. Two leads at $3 and $15 result in an average CPA of $9. But these are two completely different situations: the first lead is excellent, while the second is unprofitable.

A media buyer looks not only at the average CPA but also at the trend—how the cost of each subsequent lead changes.

teach.title: The Logic of Marginal Cost
teach.body:
**Principle:** If the first lead came in at $X, the next one should come in at $X × 1.3–1.5 at most (with a 30–50% upward deviation). If there is no next lead at a cost >$X × 2, the ad set is underperforming or the audience is being exhausted.

**Examples:**
- The first lead came in at $3 → the second should come in at a cost of up to $4–4.5. If there is no second lead at $6+ — pause the campaign; auto-resume tomorrow
- The first lead at $7 with a payout of $6 is already unprofitable from the start. If there’s no sign of improvement within 2 days—shut it down

teach.title: Non-targeted leads
teach.body:
If the leads are clearly off-target, pause the campaign or ad set immediately—don’t wait two days.

Signs of off-target leads:
- Non-existent or incorrect phone numbers
- Age or demographics do not match the target audience (confirmed by call center feedback)
- People ordered a different product or didn’t order anything at all (according to the call center)
- Very low approval rate with a normal number of leads

Why it’s important to pause immediately: Facebook learns from those who “converted.” If it learns from non-targeted leads, it will seek out even more of them. Give it a second chance tomorrow using the auto-pause feature—so the algorithm can start learning from scratch.

teach.title: Three Positive Signs That We Should Keep Going
teach.body:
1. The CPA for first conversions is lower than or close to the actual payout
2. The CPA trend is improving or remaining stable from day to day
3. The leads are qualified—the call center confirms a high approval rate

If all three conditions are met, proceed and consider scaling up.

l1.q: The first lead cost $2. How much should the second one cost?
options: $2 — the second one should cost the same
$4–5 at most—a 30–50% upward deviation is acceptable
$10 — daily budget
It doesn't matter how much—the main thing is to get it

l1.q: The first three leads are people aged 20–25, but the offer is for people 50 and older. What should I do?
options: Wait—maybe the next ones will be on target
Turn it off right away—Facebook learns from irrelevant content and will look for more of the same
Cut the budget in half
Contact the affiliate program manager

l2.situation:
Scenario — $15/day, payout upon approval of $7:

Ad Set A — two days:
Day 1: lead at $2.1, lead at $4.1, end of day $8.7 (no leads on the 3rd)
Day 2: leads at $3.4, $3.8, $4.9. Total CPA $4.0.

Ad Set B — two days:
Day 1: lead at $4.8, end-of-day total $14.2 (no second lead)
Day 2: lead at $7.1, end-of-day total $15 (no second lead)

questions.q: Is there a trend in Adseti A?
options: Bad News — CPA Is Rising
Positive — more leads per day, CPA consistently below $7
Neutral
Negative — the third lead on the first day didn't show up
Two more days
Off — two days of a single high-priced lead with no sign of improvement and an increasing number
Increase the budget to $30
Replace the CREO without shutting it down

teach.title: When to scale
teach.body:
Scale only when the following conditions are met:
- The CPA is consistently lower than the actual payout for at least 3–5 consecutive days
- The trend is either stable or improving
- Approval has been confirmed by the affiliate network

Don’t scale based on unstable results—you might just end up increasing your losses.

teach.title: Vertical scaling
teach.body:
Increasing the budget for a profitable ad set.

**Standard ad sets:** no more than 15–20% at a time, no more frequently than once every 2 days. A sharp increase can disrupt the algorithm’s learning process.

**Low-cost ads** — ads where leads are very cheap and stable (CPA is significantly lower than the payout, e.g., $2 with an $8 payout). Such ads can sometimes withstand a more aggressive increase — even doubling the budget. But be careful: test a +50% increase first, then see how it goes.

**Example of gradual scaling:**
- Day 1: $15/day, CPA $4.5 ✓
- Day 3: $18/day (+20%), CPA $4.8 ✓
- Day 5: $22/day (+22%), CPA $5.1 ✓
- Day 7: $26/day, CPA $5.3 — still profitable

teach.title: Horizontal scaling
teach.body:
Launching the same ad set on new ad accounts.

**Why this is better than duplicates within the same account:**
Duplicates within the same account compete against each other in the auction. A new account = a separate auction participant with no internal competition.

**The difference between duplicating and copying:**
- **Duplicate** — Facebook transfers accumulated training data. The new ad set starts out “smarter.”
- **Copy** — only the structure, without training data. Starts from scratch.

When scaling horizontally to a new account—you launch a new campaign but with the same settings. This is essentially a “copy” but on an isolated account—which is exactly how it should be.

teach.title: What NOT to Do When Scaling
teach.body:
- Dramatically increasing the budget (more than 30% at a time for standard ad sets)
- Changing the audience or creative at the same time as increasing the budget
- Scaling based on inconsistent results (good today, bad yesterday)
- Scaling only vertically without horizontal scaling—risk of relying on a single account

l1.q: A profitable ad set, $20/day, CPA of $5 with a payout of $8. He wants to increase it to $60 right away. Is there a problem?
options: $60 is too much
A sharp increase (300%) can disrupt the learning process and impair or destroy the results
You need to duplicate it first
You can only scale up after 50 conversions

l1.q: How is duplication different from copying?
options: Dubbing is more expensive
Duplication transfers accumulated learning experience, while copying transfers only the structure
They are the same
Copying gets results faster

l2.situation:
Situation:
Profitable ad set: $20/day, CPA of $4.5 with a payout of $7, consistently for 6 days. The goal is to reach a total daily budget of $100.

options: Raise it to $100 right away
Gradually increase by +15–20% every 2 days, and at the same time, run the same campaign on 2–3 new accounts
Duplicate the ad set 5 times in the same account
First, the new Creos

questions.q: I increased the budget from $20 to $24. The next day, the CPA rose from $4.5 to $6.8. What does this mean?
options: The connection has stopped working
The algorithm is adapting to the new budget—give it another 1–2 days before drawing any conclusions
Increasing the budget always worsens the CPA
We need to lower it back down immediately

questions.q: Why is horizontal scaling on new accounts better than duplicates in the same account?
options: Facebook limits the number of adsets in a campaign
Duplicate accounts in the same office compete against each other in the auction—new accounts do not compete, and each receives the full budget
New accounts have a higher trust score
There is no difference

lessons.title: Basic Analytics: Daily and Weekly Recap

teach.title: Why Keep Records?
teach.body:
A media buyer who doesn't keep records is someone who keeps rediscovering the same things over and over again. In two weeks, you won't remember which creative you tested, which audience you tried, or why you paused that ad set.

Notes aren’t just for memory’s sake. They help you spot patterns: “This ad set always performs worse on Mondays” or “After increasing the budget, the CPA worsens for two days and then stabilizes.”

teach.title: What to Write Down Every Day
teach.body:
Minimum Daily Report:

| Date | Ad Set | Spend | Leads | CPA | Action | Comment |
|------|-------|---------|------|-----|-----|----------|
| Mon | A-broad | $9.8 | 0 | — | Turned off creative, auto-scheduling at 12:00 AM | CTR 2.1%, suspected issue with landing page |
| Tue | A-broad | $9.5 | 2 | $4.75 | Left | Targeted leads; approval confirmed by manager |

teach.title: Weekly Roundup
teach.body:
At the end of each week (preferably on Friday or Saturday):

- Total expenses for the week
- Total attributed conversions and estimated payout
- Weekly ROI (preliminary, excluding hold)
- Which hypotheses were tested and what the results were
- Conclusions: what to scale up, what to pause, and what to test next week

teach.title: Cross-platform data reconciliation
teach.body:
**Daily:** Compare conversions in Ads Manager and in the affiliate program dashboard. If Facebook shows 20 lead events and the affiliate program shows 5 conversions, there’s a technical issue (postback, pixel, or duplicate events).

**Weekly:** Compare your total Facebook spending (from billing) with the total payouts accrued from the affiliate network.

**Remember:** Ads Manager displays attribution data (with a delay). The affiliate network shows actual conversions. A small difference (10–20%) is normal. A large difference (50%+) indicates a problem.

teach.title: Google Looker Studio for Easy Monitoring
teach.body:
A free tool from Google that lets you build dashboards by connecting data from Meta Ads Manager. It’s useful if you manage multiple accounts—you can view them all in one place without having to log in to each account separately.

Details — [→ Library: Analytics Tools]

l1.q: Why compare leads in Ads Manager and in the affiliate program?
options: To find duplicate conversions
To identify a discrepancy that indicates a technical issue—if Facebook counts 20 leads and the affiliate program counts 5, that’s critical
Affiliate programs and Facebook always show different data—that's normal
For tax reporting

l1.q: MediaBuyer relies solely on memory, without any records. The main problem:
options: Facebook may remove the statistics
Without records, it's impossible to identify patterns; mistakes are repeated, and there's no understanding of what actually produced results
The affiliate network requires reports
Without records, it is impossible to scale

questions.q: Overall, it was a losing week. What should we do about Adset A?
options: Turn off — the overall result is poor
Scale — CPA $3.78 < payouts $6, loss due to other ads
Leave as is
Replace the creosote

questions.q: What should we do with B and G?
options: One more week
Turn both off — B is unstable, D is unprofitable throughout the week
Increase the budget
Replace only the creo

questions.q: What's the plan for next week?
options: Turn everything off and start from scratch
Scale up A, test the new creative for B, disable B and D, and test 1–2 new hypotheses
Leave everything as it is
Increase the budget for all four by 50%

summary:
After completing this module, students will be able to:

- Go through the pre-launch checklist and identify issues before spending the budget
- Handle the first day correctly: what to look for, what not to touch, and when to make exceptions
- Apply the two-day rule and auto-rules
- Read the metrics funnel and identify where the chain broke
- Understand the concept of marginal lead cost and conversion dynamics
- Scale correctly: vertically in stages and horizontally to new accounts
- Track basic analytics and weekly summaries

**Next module:** Accounts, Dofarm, and security.
